decisions.title: PDF is the frozen contract
decisions.text: Reference Decisions govern: single tenant, Python-only, one-host Docker Compose, FastAPI+Pydantic v2, PostgreSQL 16 unified store, Temporal, Drain3/AST pre-processing, tiered OpenRouter routing with local Ollama, 80k tokens and USD 0.08 per incident, invariants I1-I6.

decisions.title: Minimal Python e-commerce demo app
decisions.text: Deliberately-breakable demo is a minimal Python e-commerce service matching the PDF reference scenario (deployment changes a config value, app returns HTTP 500, monitoring raises alert).

decisions.title: Mac toolchain choices
decisions.text: Colima as open-source Docker provider, uv with Python 3.12, OpenRouter key held by user in env var only, Ollama for free dev/CI.

decisions.title: Demo covers all three fault types
decisions.text: Showcase demo supports config regression, code bug, and inconclusive-evidence cases, matching the Layer 3 incident catalog.

decisions.title: Single user plays engineer and approver
decisions.text: In the showcase one human holds both engineer and approver roles via CLI and HTTP API; RBAC separation is exercised by role, not by person.

decisions.title: Checkout error-rate alert triggers showcase
decisions.text: The showcase trigger is a Prometheus error-rate alert on the demo e-commerce checkout flow delivered by Alertmanager webhook.

decisions.title: Operator-owned acceptance criteria
decisions.text: AC-7, AC-8, and AC-9 are operator-owned: toolchain setup, API key in environment, and the showcase approver role. Each is verified by an executable gate before the workflow proceeds.

decisions.title: Docker Desktop fallback on Intel macOS 26
decisions.text: Homebrew installer refuses Intel on macOS 26 (Apple-Silicon-only), so Colima via brew is uninstallable; manual Colima 0.10.3 + Lima 1.0.4 stalled on missing qemu-img (no conda-forge osx-64 build). Adopted SPEC-sanctioned fallback: Docker Desktop Intel (dmg) installed to /Applications, daemon verified via docker ps. Colima/lima/docker-cli binaries remain in ~/.local/bin.

decisions.title: BM25 for M2, hybrid deferred
decisions.text: M2-RUNBOOKS stays BM25-only: runbook corpus is small (single org/demo), BM25 needs no embedding tier and adds no model cost or latency. Hybrid (pgvector + embeddings + RRF fusion) recorded as a future learning proposal, to be promoted only if the frozen M2 retrieval baseline eval shows measured misses. Stock PostgreSQL 16 FTS is ts_rank, not BM25: M2 pre-flight must confirm the BM25 mechanism (pg_search extension or equivalent) against the one-host Compose constraint.

decisions.title: M2 BM25 in Python over PG-stored corpus
decisions.text: M2 implements BM25 ranking in stdlib Python (~30 lines, Okapi k1=1.5 b=0.75) over runbooks stored in the unified stock PostgreSQL 16 container, instead of the pg_search extension. Keeps the SPEC one-host stock-PG16 store with zero new infra; deterministic for the frozen baseline. pg_search and hybrid (pgvector) both deferred to the learning proposal if scale demands.

decisions.title: Post-M5 PDF-parity completion M6-M8
decisions.text: PDF-vs-implementation comparison 2026-11-24: M0-M5 are milestone slices; the Combined System Design (PDF pp.92-108) is partially missing (Temporal spine, canonical data model/state machines, trust-zone split, model gateway, full HTTP contract, root Compose + live alert path). Added FR-14..FR-19 and AC-10 to SPEC.md, implemented after M5 as M6-SPINE (FR-14,FR-15), M7-TRUST (FR-16,FR-18), M8-GATEWAY (FR-17,FR-19). Deviations standing: Python BM25 over PG corpus, Docker Desktop sandbox rootlessness.

knowledge.title: M6 spine gate is environment-blocked in the Marley sandbox
knowledge.text: The spine gate command (uv run pytest tests/test_spine.py) cannot complete in Marley's current sandbox: temporalio's WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping never returns there (reproduced with budgets up to 1 hour, with the test-server binary pre-downloaded, CPU ~0; the same binary runs standalone and the workflow scenario passes against a manually started server: granted->resolved, rejected->escalated). The suite's substance is verified directly: 12 of 13 tests pass under the gate's own pytest command on a fresh database, and the workflow test's exact scenario passes via the manual-server harness. The gate is expected to pass on the owner's machine or CI, where start_time_skipping worked on 2026-11-24. M7/M8 code is therefore verified by direct test runs in the sandbox and their Genesis gates are to be run where the bootstrap works.
